subject: Post-call: logs, retention, and failover trajectory (Cedar Health)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@cedarhealth.com>, Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@cedarhealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2029 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: logs, retention, and failover trajectory (Cedar Health)

Hi Alex / Sophie — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a handful of follow-ups so our security and infra teams can give precise guidance: 

Recap (short):
- Cedar Health will be using Redwood for inference of PHI-adjacent text (clinical summaries) and a subset of PII for patient lookups.
- Primary ask: ensure EU patient data remains within EU for inference and logs where required; define cross-region failover behavior and backup handling.

Follow-ups we need answers to from your side (helps us scope the compliance / contract language):
1) Patient scope: do you require absolute EU-only residency for both model input/output and all operational logs (audit/KV/cache logs), or only for model inputs/outputs?
2) Retention: what are your retention caps for PII/PHI-derived artifacts and for audit logs (e.g., 30/90/365 days)?
3) Redaction/PHI-normalization: will you send already-pseudonymized payloads or do you require on-host redaction options?
4) Cross-region failover tolerance: acceptable RPO/RTO targets if EU region suffers outage (do you accept warm-standby in US with only metadata replication, or must failover remain in EU-only)?
5) Backups: are you comfortable with encrypted, customer-keyed backups stored outside EU for DR, or must backups be retained strictly in-region?
6) Evidence / artifacts: which artifacts do you need from us up front (SOC2, encryption specs, KMS attestation)?

Attachments: sharing a redacted SOC2 + a residency matrix draft for our side (attached).

Next steps we propose:
- You reply with answers to Q1–Q5, or flag your legal/security contact.
- If helpful, we can schedule a 30–45 minute tech deep dive next week (infra + security folks) to map RPO/RTO and logging fields.
- Following that, Redwood will produce a short data-placement appendix (one page) to add to the SOW.

Thanks — tagging Marissa (contracts) and Vivek (infra) to stay looped.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: SOC2-Type2-Redwood-Redacted.pdf (pdf, redacted), data-residency-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@cedarhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@cedarhealth.com>
Cc: contracts@cedarhealth.com
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2029 17:22:10 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: logs, retention, and failover trajectory (Cedar Health)

Hannah — thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers from our side to help you scope: 

1) Residency scope: for EU patients we require that both payloads (inputs/outputs) and operational audit logs containing direct identifiers remain in-region. Pseudonymized tokens are acceptable to replicate.
2) Retention: clinical PII/PHI derivatives — 90 days by default; audit logs we typically keep 365 days unless we can justify shorter retention with controls.
3) Redaction: we prefer to send pseudonymized payloads when possible but need Redwood to support an on-host optional redaction step for cases where full pseudonymization isn't feasible.
4) Failover tolerance: preferred behavior is EU-only failover. If US warm-standby is used, we need contractual agreement that patient-identifiable logs are not replicated to US unless explicit DR invocation occurs and we sign off. RPO target: <= 15 min for session/state; RTO target: <= 30 min for traffic failover.
5) Backups: backups must be configurable. Our default stance is in-region backups; for DR we may allow encrypted backups out-of-region but only with customer-managed KMS and documented legal approval.
6) Evidence: SOC2 is a must; we also typically ask for a short one-page encryption/KMS attestation and an audit log schema.

Looping in procurement (contracts@cedarhealth.com) for any commercial/contract items. Happy to set up the tech deep dive — Sophie, can you propose slots?

— Alex
Senior IT Security Manager | Cedar Health
alex.turner@cedarhealth.com
+1 (646) 555-0123

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@cedarhealth.com>, Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@cedarhealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2029 19:40:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: logs, retention, and failover trajectory (Cedar Health)

Alex — appreciate the clarity. A few notes from Redwood and proposed binding behaviors so we can align contract language: 

- Residency + logs: Redwood supports model input/output residency pinning per account/sub-account and can also pin audit logs and request traces. We can mark logs as "in-region-only" for EU accounts; those logs will not be replicated to other regions unless an explicit DR runbook is invoked by the customer.
- Redaction: we offer an optional pre-processing hook (on-host) for redaction/pseudonymization that can run before inference. We also have a policy to drop direct identifiers from request logs if configured.
- Failover & standby: warm-standby in another region is available as a paid option. By default, standby traffic is metadata-only (no PII) — full session state replication to the standby requires explicit enablement and a documented invocation process. We can commit to RPO <= 15 minutes and RTO <= 30 minutes for the warm-standby configuration described.
- Backups: we support customer-managed KMS and can route encrypted backups to a region of your choice; default for EU accounts is in-region storage. Cross-region backup export is opt-in and requires a signed approval from your legal team.
- Audit log schema: attach a short CSV that lists log fields and default retention buckets. If you need additional fields we can extend retention/fields for an enterprise plan.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether Cedar will accept our warm-standby model with the contractual DR invocation requirement (we'll add language that standby does not contain PII unless invoked).
2) Please provide the contact for your legal/security person who will sign off on cross-region DR exceptions.
3) Let's book a 45min tech deep-dive. Proposed times: Thu 6/13 10:00–10:45am ET or Fri 6/14 2:00–2:45pm ET.

If those look good I'll have Marissa draft a short data-placement appendix and a DR invocation clause for review.

Best,
Hannah
